title: Best Sales Tax Software for Startups
summary: Compare the best sales tax software for startups on cost, contracts, and filing support, from free nexus monitoring to fully managed compliance.

Startups grow fast, which creates sales tax challenges. A startup without a finance team may not realize how a strong sales quarter or a remote hire in a new location can create new tax obligations, leaving the company vulnerable to compliance risks.


Sales tax software can solve these problems, but the right software solution depends on your growth stage, company type, and how hands-on you hope to be.


If you want registration and filing handled for you with no required annual contract,[Numeral](https://www.numeral.com/) offers[free nexus monitoring](https://www.numeral.com/product/nexus-tracking) and charges[$75 per filing](https://www.numeral.com/pricing) once you have returns to file.


**Kintsugi** offers a free plan for founders who prefer a self-service solution, while **Anrok** fits global startups, and **Stripe Tax** works for early-stage startups already billing in Stripe.


This guide provides insight into the best sales tax software for startups so you can pick the one that's right for you.

## When does a startup need sales tax software?


Sales tax software is important for any startup that may incur sales tax obligations.


A free nexus monitoring plan like Numeral's can alert you to obligations before you fall out of compliance, and Numeral's[tax calculation engine](https://www.numeral.com/product/api) integrates with all your sales platforms to ensure you charge the correct tax on every transaction.


Startups that have tax obligations across multiple states need more support, including an end-to-end compliance solution. Sales tax software can simplify and manage obligations, including registrations and recurring filings.


While a software program is not required by law, compliance is, and it can be burdensome without support.


### Four factors that shape a startup's obligations


Four primary factors determine a company's sales tax obligations. Here are the key factors that affect the compliance requirements your company is subject to:


- **Economic nexus:** The Supreme Court opened the door to[economic nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/economic-nexus) in[South Dakota v. Wayfair](https://www.numeral.com/blog/south-dakota-v-wayfair) , and states can now require you to collect sales tax once you have sufficient local economic connections. The specifics vary by state, but $100,000 in annual sales into the state or 200 total transactions is a common threshold.
- **Physical nexus:**[Physical nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/physical-nexus) was traditionally the only way to become required to collect sales tax, and[the definition is broad](https://dor.wa.gov/education/industry-guides/physical-presence-nexus) . A single local employee, items stored locally through programs like Fulfillment by Amazon, or even a trade show appearance could create physical nexus.
- **What you sell:**[SaaS](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-saas) and[digital products](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-digital-goods) are exempt in some states, but are taxable in a growing number of jurisdictions, including[California starting in 2027](https://www.numeral.com/blog/california-sb-122) . Different startups can have very different sales tax obligations depending on the products they sell.
- **Marketplace connections:** If you sell on a platform that is a[marketplace facilitator](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) , such as Amazon or eBay, the marketplace may collect and remit sales tax on your behalf. You may still have to track sales to determine if you establish nexus. However, storing inventory through[Fulfillment by Amazon](https://www.numeral.com/blog/amazon-fba-sales-tax) or similar programs can trigger physical nexus.


You must determine when you have established nexus and register, then begin filing and remitting. If you fail to register and fulfill your obligations by the deadline in each state (and sometimes within local jurisdictions), you face an[audit risk](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-audit) .

## What startups should look for in sales tax software


Startups have unique needs when choosing[sales tax software](https://www.numeral.com/blog/best-sales-tax-software) because it must fit their budgets and support future growth. Here are some key features to consider:


1. **Free until you owe:** A free monitoring plan lets you track your obligations without a monthly bill until you actually have them.
2. **No long-term contracts:** A month-to-month solution gives you the flexibility you need as your company evolves.
3. **Pricing that matches your footprint:** Per-filing pricing benefits startups that file in only a few states or don't have monthly filing obligations because their sales volume isn't high enough. Per-market subscriptions that charge monthly for each registered market can be unnecessarily expensive when you don't file monthly.
4. **Fast setup:** Startups move quickly, and you don't want sales tax to impede growth. Look for a[tool that offers integration](https://www.numeral.com/integrations) with the billing, ecommerce, accounting, and HR tools you already use, like Stripe, Shopify, QuickBooks, and Rippling.
5. **Registration included or priced clearly:** As you expand into new markets, you may quickly establish[nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-nexus) in multiple jurisdictions and must begin registering. Costs can add up quickly, and you need to know pricing without having to make a phone call every time.
6. **Support with notices:** Sales tax notices and mail from state revenue authorities often land on a founder's desk if your software solution doesn't support them. Numeral offers a virtual mailbox and responds to this correspondence on your behalf.
7. **Room to grow:** Expansion brings new responsibilities. You need a solution that can[manage exemption certificates](https://www.numeral.com/product/exemption-certificate-management) for B2B deals and support[VAT and GST](https://www.numeral.com/solutions/global) as you expand outside of the United States.
8. **Help with back exposure:** Many startups don't look into[sales tax compliance](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-compliance) until it's already a problem. You need a company that can help[clean up back exposure](https://www.numeral.com/blog/voluntary-disclosure-agreement) and limit liability.


## How sales tax affects fundraising and acquisitions


Startups need to manage sales tax exposure before it compromises fundraising or puts a potential acquisition at risk.


Investors and acquirers review sales tax exposure during[due diligence](https://burklandassociates.com/2021/07/20/would-my-startup-survive-due-diligence-part-1-sales-tax/) . If your company failed to collect tax, you may owe the full amount of unpaid liabilities even if you can't recover it from customers.


If you have unaddressed exposure, this can result in:


- [A price adjustment](https://editions.journalofaccountancy.com/publication/?i=854278&article_id=5053119&view=articleBrowser) based on the unpaid liabilities
- Escrow or a requirement to put money into an account to cover unpaid sales tax liabilities
- Delays in closing as sales tax compliance issues are resolved


If you're registered in the required jurisdictions, current on your filings, and fully compliant with your obligations, sales tax won't be an obstacle. Raising funds is simpler, and you won't incur substantial costs when problems are found during due diligence.


### What to do if your startup is already behind on sales tax


If your startup is already behind on sales tax, take a strategic approach to becoming compliant.


Don't rush to[register in every state](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-permit-registration) where you have nexus, as this could open you up to audits or back-tax charges if you have unpaid liabilities. Registering will not resolve historical liability if you delayed registering, filing, or remitting.


Instead, explore options like[voluntary disclosure agreements](https://www.numeral.com/blog/voluntary-disclosure-agreement) . You can arrange these anonymously, and they offer benefits such as a limited lookback period and a penalty waiver for voluntarily reporting unpaid liabilities.


Contact with a state can affect your eligibility for these programs, so do not register without understanding your options. For example,[California's voluntary disclosure program](https://cdtfa.ca.gov/taxes-and-fees/out-of-state.htm) is only open to out-of-state businesses that have never registered with or been contacted by the CDTFA.


Numeral can help you identify unpaid liabilities and explore solutions to limit your exposure. Our[nexus study](https://www.numeral.com/product/nexus-tracking) helps identify historical exposure. We offer options to help resolve unpaid liabilities, and we'll[register](https://www.numeral.com/product/registrations) and handle filings on your behalf once you decide on a path forward.


Some states also offer limited-time amnesty programs that let you come forward and voluntarily report unpaid tax liabilities. You can review our[sales tax amnesty programs guide](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-amnesty-programs) to explore options.


While solutions exist, it's best to stay compliant from the start. Numeral makes that effortless, so[contact us](https://www.numeral.com/demo) to learn how we can help.
